business_question: Does Nestlé's dependence on coffee as a primary input commodity create hidden exposure to climate-driven supply disruptions in Brazil?
description: Nestlé is the world's largest food and beverage company and the largest consumer of coffee globally, sourcing approximately 10% of the world's coffee supply. Brazil is the world's largest coffee producer, accounting for approximately 35-40% of global supply. Arabica coffee production in Brazil is highly sensitive to frost events (which occurred in 2021), drought, and long-term climate shifts. A material disruption to Brazilian coffee supply creates direct cost pressure on Nestlé's Nescafé and Nespresso product lines, which together represent significant operating profit. An investor holding Nestlé may not recognise that a single climate event in a single geography can materially affect margins across multiple product categories simultaneously.

asset_registry: Add Nestlé to datasets/assets.csv with sector: Consumer Staples, industry: Food Processing

Nestlé must score HIGH on supply_chain_complexity (global agricultural sourcing)
Nestlé must score MEDIUM on geographic_revenue_concentration (diversified but EM exposed)

coffee → LOCATED_IN → brazil (confidence: 0.85, evidence: Brazil 35-40% global supply)
